first: मुहूर्त्तं माप जीवेच्च नरः शुक्लेण कर्मणा ।
en: It is better to live for a moment doing pure deeds than to live for ages doing wicked deeds that harm both this world and the next.

first: गते शोको न कर्तव्यो भविष्यं नैव चिन्तयेत् ।
en: Do not grieve over the past and do not worry about the future; wise people act in the present.

first: स्वभावेन हि तुष्यन्ति देवाः सत्पुरुषाः पिता ।
en: Gods, good people and a father are pleased by a sincere nature, relatives by a bath and a drink offered to them, and the learned by good conversation.

first: आयुः कर्म च वित्तञ्च विद्या निधनमेव च ।
en: Length of life, work, wealth, learning and the time of death: these five are fixed for a being while it is still in the womb.
How wonderful are the ways of great souls! They think of wealth as mere straw, yet when they have it they bow low under its weight.

first: यस्य स्नेहो भयं तस्य स्नेहो दुःखस्य भाजनम् ।
en: Whoever has attachment has fear; attachment is the home of sorrow. All sorrows grow from attachment; give it up and live happily.
One who plans for what is coming and one who thinks quickly when trouble comes both do well; but one who says 'whatever will be, will be' is ruined.

first: राज्ञधर्मणि धर्मिष्ठाः पापे पापाः समे समाः ।
en: When the king is righteous, the people are righteous; when he is sinful, they are sinful; when he is ordinary, so are they. People follow the king: as the king is, so are his people.
I count a living person without righteousness as dead; one who dies with righteousness lives long, without doubt.
One who gains none of the four aims of life (duty, wealth, pleasure and freedom) has a birth as useless as the teats on a goat's neck.
Low people burn in the fierce fire of other people's fame; since they cannot rise to that level, they turn to speaking ill of them.
A mind attached to the pleasures of the senses leads to bondage, and a mind free of them leads to freedom; the mind alone is the cause of a person's bondage and freedom.
When pride in the body falls away through knowing the Supreme Self, then wherever the mind goes, it rests in deep meditation.

first: ईप्सितं मनसः सर्वं कस्य सम्पद्यते सुखम् ।
en: Who gets everything his heart desires? All things depend on fate, so one should rely on contentment.
As a calf finds its own mother among a thousand cows, so the deeds a person has done follow the doer.

first: अनवस्थितकार्यस्य न जने न वने सुखम् ।
en: One whose work and mind are unsettled finds no happiness among people or in the forest; people burn him with their company, and the forest burns him with loneliness.

first: यत् खनित्वा खनित्रेण भुतले वारि विन्दति ।
en: Just as one who digs the ground with a spade finds water, so a student who serves his teacher gains the learning the teacher holds.
A person's results depend on his past deeds, and his mind follows those deeds; even so, wise and noble people act only after careful thought.
One who does not honour the teacher who taught him even a single letter is born a hundred times as a dog and then among outcasts.
At the end of an age Mount Meru may move, and at the end of the world the seven seas may move; but good people never move from a promise they have made.
There are three jewels on earth: food, water and good words; fools give the name 'jewel' to pieces of stone.
